name: blade_steel
summary: A sword blade: MU's painted highlight kept, with enough real reflectance that the sun draws a second one on top of it.
why: Half a metal, which needs the argument, and the argument is a measurement.
painted_steel exists because MU's metal sheets are paintings rather than reflectances -
steel.jpg averages 0.083 linear, steel_barred_b 0.015, and iron's F0 is 0.56. Handed to a
renderer as metal those come back as black chrome, so painted_steel sets metallic 0 and
lets the painted highlight carry the whole look. That reasoning is sound and it is drawn
from armour and railing sheets.
A blade sheet is not one of those. sword06 averages 0.306 linear with 79% of its texels
above 0.3 - four times the sheet painted_steel was written against, and within sight of a
darker steel's reflectance. The measurement is the whole reason this file exists: it is
not a different opinion about MU's art, it is a different sheet.
So metallic 0.35 rather than 0 or 1. At 0 there is almost nothing for a light to do and
the blade reads as matte white plastic, which is painted_steel's own warning coming true
on a surface broad enough to see it. At 1 the diffuse goes entirely and the blade has only
the reflection probe to show, which indoors of an interior probe is the ground: rendered,
it is black end to end. At 0.35 the painted brightness survives as diffuse and the sun and
the ground arrive on top of it - a dark spine, a bright flat, and a lit line along the edge.
Roughness 0.18, tighter than painted_steel's 0.28. A blade is polished and what sells that
is a narrow highlight; broadened, the same energy spreads into the sheen that made it look
matte in the first place.
The brushed grain is painted_steel's, unchanged and for its reason: along v at scale 300,
it is the mill's mark running the length of the steel. It stripes anything broader than a
bar, so this belongs on blades and not on a shield's face.
Worth knowing that every earlier material trial on this blade - plate_steel, then steel,
then painted_steel - was run while clean_lowpoly's creases were not being marked at all,
so each was judged on a mesh shaded across its own folds. steel was retried here under
correct shading and is still black, which is the one of the three that the fix did not
change. See Sword05's creases_from.
